text:
### Observed differences

- **A01 now appears as an isolated first step instead of a mid-cycle step.** In the earlier window A01 appeared in about 21 in 100 traces, around two-thirds into the trace (median relative position 0.7), and all 74 of its observed outgoing transitions led to A09. In the later window A01 appears in about 34 in 100 traces, every occurrence sits at the very first position (median 0.0), no outgoing transition was ever observed from it, and it no longer shares a trace with A04, A05, A08, A09, A13, A16 or A17 — co-occurrence fell from about 8–21 in 100 traces to zero for all seven partners, and repetition of A01 within a trace disappeared. [OCC001, DIR001, POS001, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007]

- **A17, not observed before (0 of 200 traces), now takes part in the cycle.** In the later window it occurs in about 13 in 100 traces at a similar mid-late position A01 used to hold (median about 0.71), every one of its 51 observed executions leads to A09, and it co-occurs with A04, A08, A09, A13 and A16 in roughly 10–13 in 100 traces. [OCC017, DIR012, POS008, REL013, REL022, REL025, REL027, REL028]

- **The repeating cycle runs through different activities.** Earlier, A16 always led to A05, A05 led to A01 (about 54% of its outgoing transitions) or back to A16, A09 led mainly to A06 (47%) or A08 (43%), and A08 led back to A13 (53%) or A04 (47%). In the later window A16 always leads to A08, A08 leads to A16 (51%) or A17 (49%), A09 leads mainly to A05 (51%) or A06 (33%), and A05 — now seen in only about 6 in 100 traces, down from 21 — leads to A13 (54%) or A04 (46%). [DIR003, DIR006, DIR007, DIR009, DIR011, OCC005]

- **Step distances match the new wiring.** A08 now reaches A09 about 2 steps later (before: about 5), A09 reaches A05 directly (before: about 4 steps), A04 and A13 reach A08 within 1–2 steps (before: 4–5), A08 reaches A04 or A13 only after 4–5 steps (before: 1–2), and A16 and A08, about 4 steps apart before, now follow one another directly. [LAG014, LAG018, LAG003, LAG023, LAG012, LAG015, LAG016, LAG028]

- **Occurrence levels moved with the rewiring.** A05's mean occurrences per trace fell from 0.68 to 0.13 while A08's rose from 0.16 to 0.52; A04 and A13 became less frequent (participation about 21 down to 12–13 in 100 traces, A04's recurrence support 0.145 to 0.105), as did A09 (about 21 down to 12–13 in 100). [OCC005, OCC008, OCC004, OCC013, OCC009]

- **Participation also fell for activities outside these edges.** A02 (about 50 down to 38 in 100 traces), A03 (29 down to 16), A06 (21 down to 12), A12 (10 down to 7) and A18 (10 down to 6) declined, with smaller declines for A07, A10 and A16, while A14 and A15 stayed flat. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC006, OCC012, OCC018, OCC007, OCC010, OCC016, OCC014, OCC015]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the repeating cycle was restructured and A01 was moved out of it to the start of separate traces. In the earlier window the cycle ran A16 → A05 → A01 → A09 → A08 → A04/A13 and returned to A05, with A01 embedded in the middle; in the later window A01 starts its own traces in isolation (first position, no observed successor, no shared traces with any cycle activity), A17 has appeared in the slot A01 used to occupy, and A05 and A08 have traded roles, so the cycle runs A16 → A08 → A17 (or back to A16) → A09 → A05 → A04/A13 → back to A08. This rests on direct evidence from three indicator families at once: five complete successor replacements (A16: A05→A08; A08: A13/A04→A16/A17; A09: A08→A05; A05: A01/A16→A13/A04; the new A17→A09), each backed by 26–136 transitions and each more extreme than in about 199 of 200 random re-splits of unchanged data; seven pair relations in which regular co-occurrence with A01 (about 8–21 in 100 traces) drops to exactly zero while A01's own participation rises to about 34 in 100, which random sampling cannot plausibly produce; A01's position distribution moving from a median of 0.7 to 0.0 in every later occurrence; and lag shifts that quantitatively match the new edges. Limitations: the windows are finite samples, so exact routing shares (for example A08's 51/49 split between A16 and A17) carry sampling uncertainty; A01's later context is only partly observable because no outgoing transition or co-occurrence was recorded for it; and no screening baseline was provided, so the qualifying items could not be compared against a formal chance expectation — the judgement rests on the directness and coherence of the relational, positional and successor evidence. An important competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is a shift in the mix of trace variants (for example a new variant containing A17 and isolated A01 traces displacing an old variant) rather than a rewiring of one process; the behavioural description above holds under either reading. [DIR001, DIR003, DIR006, DIR007, DIR009, DIR011, DIR012, POS001, POS008, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, OCC001, OCC005, OCC008, OCC017, LAG003, LAG012, LAG014, LAG015, LAG016, LAG018, LAG023, LAG028]

Other differences: Participation in A02, A03, A06, A12 and A18 fell (for example A02 from about 50 to 38 in 100 traces, A03 from about 29 to 16), with smaller declines for A07, A10 and A16; the evidence shows these declines but does not show how they connect to the cycle rewiring described above. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC006, OCC012, OCC018, OCC007, OCC010, OCC016]
